source.text: וֶאֱלִישָׁע֙ הַנָּבִ֔יא קָרָ֕א לְאַחַ֖ד מִבְּנֵ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר ל֜וֹ חֲגֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֗יךָ וְ֠קַח פַּ֣ךְ הַשֶּׁ֤מֶן הַזֶּה֙ בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ וְלֵ֖ךְ רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And Elisha the prophet called to one of [the] sons of the prophets and said to him, Gird up your loins and take [the] flask of the oil this in your hand and go [to] Ramoth-gilead.

en.L: And Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, "Gird up your loins, and take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
en.B: Elisha the prophet called one of the company of prophets and said to him, "Tuck your robe into your belt, take this flask of oil with you, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
en.R: Elisha the prophet called a man from the group of prophets. He said to him, "Get ready to travel. Take this small jar of olive oil with you and go to the town of Ramoth-gilead.

decisions.choice: sons of the prophets: a member of a band of prophets
decisions.reason: "Sons of" means members of a group, not children. These prophets lived and worked together, and Elisha led them as Elijah had before him (2:3, 15; 4:38; 6:1).

decisions.choice: gird up your loins: get ready to move quickly
decisions.reason: Men wore long robes. Before running or hard work they pulled up the lower part and tucked it into the belt (1 Kings 18:46; 2 Kings 4:29). The order means "go at once, and go fast".

decisions.choice: the flask of oil: a small vessel of anointing oil
decisions.reason: The word names a small jar or flask, the same word used for the oil Samuel poured on Saul (1 Samuel 10:1). Pouring oil on a man's head set him apart as king (1 Samuel 16:13; 1 Kings 1:39).

decisions.choice: Ramoth-gilead: the frontier town where Israel's army faced Aram
decisions.reason: Ramoth-gilead, east of the Jordan, was fought over by Israel and Aram (1 Kings 22:3). Joram king of Israel had been wounded there and had gone back to Jezreel, leaving his commanders with the army (8:28-29; 9:14-15).

decisions.choice: sons of the prophets (Literal); company of prophets (Balanced); group of prophets (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 2:3: the wording follows the settled terms for Samuel and Kings.

decisions.choice: tuck your robe into your belt (Balanced); get ready to travel (Readable); small jar of olive oil (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom; Balanced says what the man did, as in 1 Kings 18:46, and Readable gives its point. Readable also says what kind of oil and vessel it was.

source.text: וּבָ֖אתָ שָׁ֑מָּה וּרְאֵֽה־שָׁ֠ם יֵה֨וּא בֶן־יְהוֹשָׁפָ֜ט בֶּן־נִמְשִׁ֗י וּבָ֨אתָ֙ וַהֲקֵֽמֹתוֹ֙ מִתּ֣וֹךאֶחָ֔יו וְהֵבֵיאתָ֥ אֹת֖וֹ חֶ֥דֶר בְּחָֽדֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will come there and see there Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi, and you will go in and make him rise from among his brothers and bring him [into a] room within a room.

en.L: And when you come there, look there for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi, and go in and make him get up from among his brothers, and bring him into an inner room.
en.B: When you get there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi. Go in, have him get up from among his fellow officers, and take him into an inner room.
en.R: When you get there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat and grandson of Nimshi. Go in and call him away from the other officers. Take him to a room where you can be alone.

decisions.choice: Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi: Jehu's father and grandfather
decisions.reason: Jehu's father was Jehoshaphat, not the king of Judah with that name, and Nimshi was his grandfather. Elsewhere Jehu is often called simply "son of Nimshi" (verse 20; 1 Kings 19:16), naming him by the better-known ancestor.

decisions.choice: his brothers: his fellow officers
decisions.reason: "Brothers" here means comrades, the other commanders of the army sitting with him (verse 5), not his family.

decisions.choice: a room within a room: an inner, private room
decisions.reason: The doubled word means a room inside the house, away from others (1 Kings 20:30; 22:25). The anointing was to be done in secret.

decisions.choice: fellow officers (Balanced); the other officers (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "brothers" in this setting (m2).

decisions.choice: and grandson of Nimshi
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that Nimshi was Jehu's grandfather, since verse 20 calls Jehu "son of Nimshi".

source.text: וְלָקַחְתָּ֤ פַךְ־הַשֶּׁ֨מֶן֙ וְיָצַקְתָּ֣ עַל־רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מְשַׁחְתִּ֥יךָֽ לְמֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּפָתַחְתָּ֥ הַדֶּ֛לֶת וְנַ֖סְתָּה וְלֹ֥א תְחַכֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take [the] flask of the oil and pour on his head and say, Thus says Yahweh, I have anointed you to king over Israel; and you will open the door and flee and not wait.

en.L: And take the flask of oil and pour [it] on his head and say, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: I anoint you king over Israel.' Then open the door and flee, and do not wait."
en.B: Then pour the flask of oil over his head and say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I anoint you king over Israel.' After that, open the door and run; do not wait."
en.R: Then pour the oil on his head and say, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am making you king over Israel.' Then open the door and run away. Do not stay there."

decisions.choice: I anoint you: the anointing takes effect as the words are spoken
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for a completed act, used when a speaker brings something about by saying it. Yahweh, through the prophet, makes Jehu king at that moment.

decisions.choice: I anoint you king over Israel: the charge given to Elijah carried out
decisions.reason: At Horeb Yahweh told Elijah to anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king over Israel (1 Kings 19:16-17). Elisha now has it done through one of the prophets.

decisions.choice: open the door and flee: leave at once
decisions.reason: The messenger is not to stay to talk or explain. To be found anointing a rival king in the army's camp was dangerous, and the haste also leaves Jehu alone with the word of Yahweh.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (Literal); The LORD says this (Balanced); This is what the LORD says (Readable)
decisions.reason: The prophetic formula is worded as everywhere in Samuel and Kings.

decisions.choice: I am making you king
decisions.reason: Readable says what anointing does here, since "anoint" is not an everyday word.

source.text: וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ הַנַּ֛עַר הַנַּ֥עַר הַנָּבִ֖יא רָמֹ֥ת גִּלְעָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And went the young man, the young man the prophet, [to] Ramoth-gilead.

en.L: And the young man, the young man the prophet, went to Ramoth-gilead.
en.B: So the young man, the prophet's servant, went to Ramoth-gilead.
en.R: So the young man, the prophet's helper, went to Ramoth-gilead.

decisions.choice: the young man, the young man the prophet: the prophet's young servant
alternatives: the young man, the young prophet
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "the young man" and then adds "the prophet". It most likely means "the young man, the servant of the prophet", that is, Elisha's young helper (compare 5:20). It could also mean "the young man, the young prophet", one of the company of prophets (verse 1).

decisions.choice: the prophet's servant (Balanced); the prophet's helper (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the more likely sense (m1); Literal keeps the repeated words.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֗א וְהִנֵּ֨ה שָׂרֵ֤י הַחַ֨יִל֙ יֹֽשְׁבִ֔ים וַיֹּ֕אמֶר דָּבָ֥ר לִ֛י אֵלֶ֖יךָ הַשָּׂ֑ר וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יֵהוּא֙ אֶל־מִ֣י מִכֻּלָּ֔נוּ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלֶ֥יךָ הַשָּֽׂר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he came, and behold, [the] commanders of the army [were] sitting; and he said, A word [is] to me for you, the commander; and said Jehu, For whom of all of us? And he said, For you, the commander.

en.L: And he came, and look, the commanders of the army [were] sitting [there]. And he said, "I have a word for you, commander." And Jehu said, "For which of all of us?" And he said, "For you, commander."
en.B: When he arrived, the commanders of the army were sitting together. He said, "I have a message for you, commander." Jehu asked, "For which one of us?" He answered, "For you, commander."
en.R: When he got there, the army commanders were sitting together. He said, "Sir, I have a message for you." "For which one of us?" Jehu asked. "For you, sir," he answered.

decisions.choice: the commanders of the army: the officers leading Israel's troops
decisions.reason: They were holding Ramoth-gilead against Hazael king of Aram while King Joram was away (verse 14).

decisions.choice: commander: a respectful address
decisions.reason: The young man speaks to the group without naming anyone, so Jehu asks whom he means. His answer singles Jehu out in front of the others.

decisions.choice: a word: a message
decisions.reason: The word can mean a matter, a word or a message; here it is the message from Yahweh (verse 6).

decisions.choice: sir
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday polite form of address in place of "commander".

source.text: וַיָּ֨קָם֙ וַיָּבֹ֣א הַבַּ֔יְתָה וַיִּצֹ֥ק הַשֶּׁ֖מֶן אֶל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מְשַׁחְתִּ֧יךָֽ לְמֶ֛לֶךְ אֶל־עַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he arose and went into the house, and he poured the oil on his head and said to him, Thus says Yahweh [the] God of Israel, I have anointed you to king over [the] people of Yahweh, over Israel.

en.L: And he got up and went into the house, and he poured the oil on his head and said to him, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: I anoint you king over the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, over Israel.
en.B: Jehu got up and went into the house. The young man poured the oil on his head and said to him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: I anoint you king over the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, over Israel.
en.R: Jehu got up and went into the house with him. The young man poured the oil on Jehu's head and said, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: I am making you king over Israel, the people who belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: he got up and went into the house: Jehu
decisions.reason: The one who gets up is Jehu, called away from the others (verse 2); the young man then pours the oil. The Hebrew does not change the name of the subject.

decisions.choice: the people of Yahweh, over Israel: Israel still belongs to Yahweh
decisions.reason: The prophet's words go beyond what Elisha told him to say (verse 3). They remind Jehu that the kingdom he will rule is Yahweh's people, though its kings had led it to worship Baal.

decisions.choice: I anoint you: as in verse 3
decisions.reason: The anointing takes effect as Yahweh's words are spoken.

decisions.choice: The young man poured
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who does each act, since the Hebrew "he" changes from Jehu to the young man (m1).

decisions.choice: king over Israel, the people who belong to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable puts the familiar name first and explains "the people of the LORD".

source.text: וְהִ֨כִּיתָ֔ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית אַחְאָ֖ב אֲדֹנֶ֑יךָ וְנִקַּמְתִּ֞י דְּמֵ֣י׀עֲבָדַ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֗ים וּדְמֵ֛י כָּל־עַבְדֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מִיַּ֥ד אִיזָֽבֶל׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will strike down [the] house of Ahab your master, and I will avenge [the] blood of my slaves the prophets and [the] blood of all [the] slaves of Yahweh from [the] hand of Jezebel.

en.L: And you will strike down the house of Ahab your master, and I will avenge the blood of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slaves the prophets and the blood of all the slaves of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, from the hand of Jezebel.
en.B: You are to strike down the house of your master Ahab, and so I will avenge on Jezebel the blood of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets, and of all who serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: You will destroy the family of Ahab, your master. In this way I will punish Jezebel for killing {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants the prophets and all the other servants of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: you will strike down: a charge as well as a prediction
decisions.reason: The verb form can foretell what Jehu will do or tell him what he must do. In this commission it is both.

decisions.choice: the house of Ahab: Ahab's family line, his dynasty
decisions.reason: "House" means the royal family. Ahab was dead (1 Kings 22:37), but his son Joram was king and his widow Jezebel still had power.

decisions.choice: the blood of my servants the prophets ... from the hand of Jezebel: the prophets she killed
decisions.reason: Jezebel had killed the prophets of Yahweh (1 Kings 18:4, 13; 19:10), and she had Naboth put to death (1 Kings 21:8-15). Yahweh will demand their blood back from her, that is, punish her for their deaths.

decisions.choice: I will avenge: Yahweh speaks again in the first person
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks Yahweh's words as Yahweh's own. Jehu's sword is the means; the vengeance is Yahweh's.

decisions.choice: slaves (Literal); servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word for servant follows the settled rule: "slave" at Literal, "servant" at Balanced and Readable. Here it names those who belong to Yahweh and serve him.

decisions.choice: avenge on Jezebel (Balanced); punish Jezebel for killing (Readable)
decisions.reason: "From the hand of" means "from the one responsible". Balanced and Readable say plainly that Jezebel shed the blood.

source.text: וְאָבַ֖ד כָּל־בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֑ב וְהִכְרַתִּ֤י לְאַחְאָב֙ מַשְׁתִּ֣ין בְּקִ֔יר וְעָצ֥וּר וְעָז֖וּב בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And will perish all [the] house of Ahab, and I will cut off to Ahab one urinating against a wall, and shut up and left in Israel.

en.L: And the whole house of Ahab will perish, and I will cut off from Ahab [everyone] who urinates against a wall, both bond and free in Israel.
en.B: The whole house of Ahab will perish. From Ahab I will cut off every male in Israel, whether bond or free.
en.R: All of Ahab's family will die. I will destroy every man and boy in Ahab's family in Israel, whether slave or free.

decisions.choice: the same sentence as on Jeroboam's and Ahab's houses
decisions.reason: These are the words Ahijah spoke against Jeroboam (1 Kings 14:10) and Elijah against Ahab (1 Kings 21:21). Jehu is the one who will carry them out.

decisions.choice: one who urinates against a wall: a male
decisions.reason: The coarse phrase means every male, from the boy upward, as in 1 Samuel 25:22 and 1 Kings 14:10; 21:21.

decisions.choice: shut up and left: everyone, of every kind
decisions.reason: The meaning of the pair is not certain. It may mean slave and free, those under restraint and those at liberty, or minors under care and adults. In every reading it means all without exception (1 Kings 14:10; 21:21).

decisions.choice: every male (Balanced); every man and boy (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 21:21: Balanced and Readable give the plain sense of the coarse idiom (m2), and Literal keeps its picture. No gender setting is used, because only males are meant.

decisions.choice: bond and free (Literal, Balanced); slave or free (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 21:21; the footnote gives the other possible senses (m3).

source.text: וְנָֽתַתִּי֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֔ב כְּבֵ֖ית יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־נְבָ֑ט וּכְבֵ֖ית בַּעְשָׁ֥א בֶן־אֲחִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make [the] house of Ahab like [the] house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like [the] house of Baasha son of Ahijah.

en.L: And I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
en.B: I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
en.R: I will do to Ahab's family what I did to the families of Jeroboam son of Nebat and of Baasha son of Ahijah.

decisions.choice: the house of Jeroboam, the house of Baasha: two royal families wiped out
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 21:22: Baasha killed Jeroboam's whole family (1 Kings 15:29), and Zimri killed Baasha's (1 Kings 16:11-12). Ahab's line will end the same way.

decisions.choice: I will do to Ahab's family what I did to
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 21:22: Readable states the comparison as an action.

source.text: וְאֶת־אִיזֶ֜בֶל יֹאכְל֧וּ הַכְּלָבִ֛ים בְּחֵ֥לֶק יִזְרְעֶ֖אל וְאֵ֣ין קֹבֵ֑ר וַיִּפְתַּ֥ח הַדֶּ֖לֶת וַיָּנֹֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: And Jezebel will eat the dogs in [the] plot of ground of Jezreel, and there is no one burying; and he opened the door and fled.

en.L: And Jezebel the dogs will eat in the plot of ground of Jezreel, and there will be none to bury [her]." And he opened the door and fled.
en.B: As for Jezebel, the dogs will eat her on the plot of ground at Jezreel, and no one will bury her." Then he opened the door and ran.
en.R: Dogs will eat Jezebel's body on the land at Jezreel, and no one will bury her." Then the young man opened the door and ran away.

decisions.choice: the dogs will eat Jezebel: Elijah's word against her
decisions.reason: Elijah had said, "The dogs will eat Jezebel by the rampart of Jezreel" (1 Kings 21:23). Here the place is "the plot of ground of Jezreel", the same words Jehu uses when the word comes true (verses 36-37).

decisions.choice: plot of ground: a portion of land
decisions.reason: The word means a share or portion, here the land around the town of Jezreel. It is close to the word for Naboth's plot in verses 21, 25 and 26, and Jezebel's death on this ground matches the field she had seized for Ahab.

decisions.choice: there will be none to bury her: the worst disgrace
decisions.reason: To lie unburied and be eaten by dogs was the deepest shame and a sign of a curse (1 Kings 14:11; 21:24; Jeremiah 22:19). Verses 34-35 tell how it happened.

decisions.choice: plot of ground (Literal, Balanced); the land at Jezreel (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the portion of land (m2).

source.text: וְיֵה֗וּא יָצָא֙ אֶל־עַבְדֵ֣י אֲדֹנָ֔יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הֲשָׁל֔וֹם מַדּ֛וּעַ בָּֽא־הַמְשֻׁגָּ֥ע הַזֶּ֖ה אֵלֶ֑יךָ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אַתֶּ֛ם יְדַעְתֶּ֥ם אֶת־הָאִ֖ישׁ וְאֶת־שִׂיחֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Jehu went out to [the] servants of his master, and one said to him, [Is it] peace? Why came this madman to you? And he said to them, You know the man and his talk.

en.L: And Jehu went out to the servants of his master, and [one] said to him, "Is it peace? Why did this madman come to you?" And he said to them, "You know the man and his talk."
en.B: When Jehu came out to his master's officers, one of them asked him, "Is all well? Why did this madman come to you?" He told them, "You know the man and the way he talks."
en.R: When Jehu came back out to the other officers of the king, one of them asked him, "Is everything all right? What did that crazy man want with you?" Jehu answered, "You know that kind of man and the kind of things he says."

decisions.choice: is it peace?: is all well?
decisions.reason: The word for peace means wholeness and well-being. As a question it asks whether all is well (4:26; 5:21). The same question is asked again and again in this chapter (verses 17-22, 31), where it asks whether Jehu comes as a friend or an enemy.

decisions.choice: this madman: a scornful name for a prophet
decisions.reason: The officers call the prophet a man who is out of his mind, perhaps because of his strange haste or the way prophets behaved (1 Samuel 10:10-11; Jeremiah 29:26; Hosea 9:7). The same root is used of Jehu's wild driving in verse 20.

decisions.choice: you know the man and his talk: Jehu brushes the question aside
decisions.reason: Jehu suggests they know what such men are like and what they say, as if the visit meant nothing, or that they had sent the man themselves. The officers do not accept the answer (verse 12).

decisions.choice: his master's officers (Balanced); the other officers of the king (Readable)
decisions.reason: The king's "servants" are his officers, as in Samuel and Kings: Literal keeps "servants", and Balanced and Readable say "officers" since these are army commanders.

decisions.choice: Is all well? (Balanced); Is everything all right? (Readable)
decisions.reason: Here the question is the officers' concern about the visit (m1). In verses 17-31 it is asked of someone approaching, and is worded "Is it peace?" (Literal, Balanced) and "Do you come in peace?" (Readable) every time.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ שֶׁ֔קֶר הַגֶּד־נָ֖א לָ֑נוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כָּזֹ֤את וְכָזֹאת֙ אָמַ֤ר אֵלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה מְשַׁחְתִּ֥יךָֽ לְמֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said, Falsehood! Tell please to us. And he said, Like this and like this he said to me, saying, Thus says Yahweh, I have anointed you to king over Israel.

en.L: And they said, "A lie! Tell us, please." And he said, "Like this and like this he spoke to me, saying, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: I anoint you king over Israel.'"
en.B: But they said, "That is not true! Tell us." So he said, "This is what he told me: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I anoint you king over Israel.'"
en.R: "That is not the truth!" they said. "Tell us what he said." So Jehu told them, "He said to me, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am making you king over Israel.'"

decisions.choice: a lie: you are not telling us the truth
decisions.reason: The single word is an exclamation: the officers will not accept Jehu's evasive answer and press him to tell them.

decisions.choice: like this and like this: this is what he said
decisions.reason: The repeated phrase sums up the man's speech without repeating it all (compare 5:4); Jehu then gives its heart, the words of Yahweh.

decisions.choice: I anoint you: as in verse 3
decisions.reason: Jehu repeats the words Elisha gave the young man.

decisions.choice: This is what he told me (Balanced); He said to me (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the summary phrase (m2); Literal keeps it.

source.text: וַֽיְמַהֲר֗וּ וַיִּקְחוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ בִּגְד֔וֹ וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ תַחְתָּ֖יו אֶל־גֶּ֣רֶם הַֽמַּעֲל֑וֹת וַֽיִּתְקְעוּ֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ מָלַ֥ךְ יֵהֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And they hurried and took each his garment and put [it] under him on [the] bare [part of] the steps, and they blew on the trumpet and said, Is king Jehu!

en.L: And they hurried and took each man his garment and put [it] under him on the bare steps, and they blew the trumpet and said, "Jehu is king!"
en.B: At once each man took off his cloak and spread it under Jehu on the bare steps. They blew the ram's horn and shouted, "Jehu is king!"
en.R: Right away each of them took off his coat and spread it on the steps for Jehu to stand on. Then they blew a trumpet and shouted, "Jehu is king!"

decisions.choice: each man spread his garment under him: honoring him as king
decisions.reason: Spreading cloaks under someone was a sign of homage, laying down the way for a king (compare Matthew 21:8). The officers declare their loyalty to Jehu at once.

decisions.choice: the bare steps: the steps themselves, uncertain
decisions.reason: The first word usually means "bone" and may here mean the bare stone of the steps, or the top of the stairs, where Jehu could be seen as on a throne. The exact sense is not known.

decisions.choice: they blew the trumpet and said, Jehu is king: the public proclamation of a new king
decisions.reason: The ram's horn and the shout announced a new king, as for Absalom (2 Samuel 15:10) and Solomon (1 Kings 1:34, 39).

decisions.choice: trumpet (Literal, Readable); ram's horn (Balanced)
decisions.reason: As in Judges 6:34 and 1 Kings 1:34: Literal and Readable use the familiar word, and Balanced names the instrument.

decisions.choice: for Jehu to stand on
decisions.reason: Readable says why the cloaks were spread under him.

source.text: וַיִּתְקַשֵּׁ֗ר יֵה֛וּא בֶּן־יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בֶּן־נִמְשִׁ֖י אֶל־יוֹרָ֑ם וְיוֹרָם֩ הָיָ֨ה שֹׁמֵ֜ר בְּרָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֗ד ה֚וּא וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִפְּנֵ֥י חֲזָאֵ֖ל מֶֽלֶךְ־אֲרָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And conspired Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi against Joram; and Joram had been keeping [watch] at Ramoth-gilead, he and all Israel, from before Hazael king of Aram.

en.L: So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. Now Joram had been keeping guard at Ramoth-gilead, he and all Israel, against Hazael king of Aram,
en.B: So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi plotted against Joram. Joram and all Israel had been holding Ramoth-gilead against Hazael king of Aram,
en.R: So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat and grandson of Nimshi made plans to overthrow King Joram. Joram and the whole army of Israel had been guarding the town of Ramoth-gilead against Hazael, the king of Aram.

decisions.choice: conspired: formed a plot against the king
decisions.reason: The verb is used of plots to kill a king and take the throne (1 Kings 15:27; 16:9). Jehu acts on the prophet's word, but by the means of a palace revolt.

decisions.choice: Joram had been keeping guard: background to the story
decisions.reason: Verses 14b-15a go back to explain the situation already told in 8:28-29: Joram had held Ramoth-gilead against Aram, been wounded and gone to Jezreel to recover.

decisions.choice: Joram: the son of Ahab, king of Israel
decisions.reason: Joram (also spelled Jehoram in verses 15, 17 and elsewhere) was Ahab's son and king of Israel (3:1). Ahaziah king of Judah, his nephew, had joined him (8:28-29).

decisions.choice: a full stop at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The background sentence runs on into verse 15, so Literal and Balanced end the verse with a comma; Readable makes it a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: made plans to overthrow King Joram
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "conspired" meant here.

source.text: וַיָּשָׁב֩ יְהוֹרָ֨ם הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְהִתְרַפֵּ֣א בִיְזְרְעֶ֗אל מִן־הַמַּכִּים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יַכֻּ֣הוּ אֲרַמִּ֔ים בְּהִלָּ֣חֲמ֔וֹ אֶת־חֲזָאֵ֖ל מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֑ם וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יֵהוּא֙ אִם־יֵ֣שׁ נַפְשְׁכֶ֔ם אַל־יֵצֵ֤א פָלִיט֙ מִן־הָעִ֔יר לָלֶ֖כֶת לְהַגִּ֥יד בְּיִזְרְעֶֽאל׃

records.literal_gloss: and returned Joram the king to get himself healed in Jezreel from the wounds which struck him [the] Arameans in his fighting with Hazael king of Aram. And said Jehu, If is your mind, let not go out an escapee from the city to go to tell in Jezreel.

en.L: but King Jehoram had returned to be healed in Jezreel from the wounds that the Arameans had struck him with when he fought with Hazael king of Aram. And Jehu said, "If this is your will, let no survivor go out from the city to go and tell [it] in Jezreel."
en.B: but King Jehoram had gone back to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Arameans had given him when he fought Hazael king of Aram. Jehu said, "If you are with me, do not let anyone slip out of the city to go and tell the news in Jezreel."
en.R: But King Jehoram had gone back to the town of Jezreel to get better from the wounds the Arameans gave him in the battle against Hazael. Jehu said to the officers, "If you agree with me, do not let anyone leave the city to go and warn the people in Jezreel."

decisions.choice: to tell: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) and the form marked to be read aloud (qere) of this word differ only in spelling; the meaning is the same. The king's name is spelled here in its full form, Jehoram, and in verse 14 in its short form, Joram; both name the same man.

decisions.choice: if this is your will: if you are of one mind with me
decisions.reason: The phrase uses the word for a person's inner self or desire (Genesis 23:8). Jehu asks the officers to commit themselves to his cause.

decisions.choice: let no survivor go out: let no one escape to give warning
decisions.reason: The word means someone who escapes. Jehu wants to reach Jezreel before anyone can warn Jehoram.

decisions.choice: If you are with me (Balanced); If you agree with me (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (m2).

source.text: וַיִּרְכַּ֤ב יֵהוּא֙ וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ יִזְרְעֶ֔אלָה כִּ֥י יוֹרָ֖ם שֹׁכֵ֣ב שָׁ֑מָּה וַֽאֲחַזְיָה֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה יָרַ֖ד לִרְא֥וֹת אֶת־יוֹרָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And rode Jehu and went to Jezreel, for Joram [was] lying there; and Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram.

en.L: And Jehu rode [in a chariot] and went to Jezreel, for Joram was lying there; and Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram.
en.B: Then Jehu got into his chariot and set out for Jezreel, because Joram was lying ill there, and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to visit Joram.
en.R: Then Jehu got into his chariot and drove to Jezreel. King Joram was lying there, still hurt. Ahaziah, the king of Judah, had come down to visit him.

decisions.choice: rode: drove in his chariot
decisions.reason: The verb means to ride, here in a chariot (verses 20, 24).

decisions.choice: Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram: the two kings were together
decisions.reason: Ahaziah was Ahab's grandson through his mother Athaliah (8:26-27) and had fought beside Joram (8:28-29). He was visiting his wounded uncle, and so was in Jezreel when Jehu came.

decisions.choice: lying ill there (Balanced); still hurt (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Lying" means he was in bed with his wounds (verse 15); Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: וְהַצֹּפֶה֩ עֹמֵ֨ד עַֽל־הַמִּגְדָּ֜ל בְּיִזְרְעֶ֗אל וַיַּ֞רְא אֶת־שִׁפְעַ֤ת יֵהוּא֙ בְּבֹא֔וֹ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שִׁפְעַ֖ת אֲנִ֣י רֹאֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹרָ֗ם קַ֥ח רַכָּ֛ב וּֽשְׁלַ֥ח לִקְרָאתָ֖ם וְיֹאמַ֥ר הֲשָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the watchman [was] standing on the tower in Jezreel, and he saw [the] company of Jehu in his coming, and he said, A company I [am] seeing. And said Joram, Take a horseman and send to meet them, and let him say, [Is it] peace?

en.L: And the watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel, and he saw the company of Jehu as he came, and he said, "I see a company." And Jehoram said, "Take a horseman and send [him] to meet them, and let him say, 'Is it peace?'"
en.B: The watchman standing on the tower in Jezreel saw Jehu's troop coming, and he said, "I see a troop of men." Jehoram said, "Get a horseman and send him to meet them, and have him ask, 'Is it peace?'"
en.R: A guard was standing on the watchtower in Jezreel. He saw Jehu and his men coming and called out, "I see a group of soldiers coming!" King Jehoram said, "Send a man on a horse to meet them. Have him ask, 'Do you come in peace?'"

decisions.choice: company: a band of men
decisions.reason: The word means a crowd or mass. From the tower the watchman can see a body of riders and chariots, but not yet who they are.

decisions.choice: is it peace?: do you come as friends?
decisions.reason: The question asks whether the riders come peacefully. Jehoram fears news from the war with Aram or a threat. The question is repeated in verses 18, 19, 22 and 31, and its answer grows sharper each time.

decisions.choice: a horseman: a rider
decisions.reason: The word can mean a charioteer or a horseman; verse 18 makes clear he rode a horse.

decisions.choice: Is it peace? (Literal, Balanced); Do you come in peace? (Readable)
decisions.reason: The question keeps one wording at each level through the chapter (verses 17-22, 31), so that the reader hears it repeated as the Hebrew does. Readable says what it asks.

source.text: וַיֵּלֶךְ֩ רֹכֵ֨ב הַסּ֜וּס לִקְרָאת֗וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הֲשָׁל֔וֹם וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יֵה֛וּא מַה־לְּךָ֥ וּלְשָׁל֖וֹם סֹ֣ב אֶֽל־אַחֲרָ֑י וַיַּגֵּ֤ד הַצֹּפֶה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּֽא־הַמַּלְאָ֥ךְ עַד־הֵ֖ם וְלֹֽא־שָֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: And went the rider of the horse to meet him and said, Thus says the king, [Is it] peace? And said Jehu, What [is it] to you and to peace? Turn to behind me. And reported the watchman, saying, Came the messenger to them and not returned.

en.L: And the rider on the horse went to meet him and said, "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" And Jehu said, "What [is it] to you and to peace? Turn around behind me." And the watchman reported, saying, "The messenger came to them, but he has not returned."
en.B: So the horseman went to meet Jehu and said, "The king says this: 'Is it peace?'" Jehu said, "What business of yours is peace? Fall in behind me." The watchman reported, "The messenger has reached them, but he is not coming back."
en.R: So the man rode out to meet Jehu and said, "The king asks, 'Do you come in peace?'" Jehu answered, "What does peace matter to you? Turn around and follow me." The guard on the tower reported, "The messenger reached them, but he is not coming back."

decisions.choice: what is it to you and to peace?: peace is not your business
decisions.reason: The idiom asks what a person has to do with something (Judges 11:12; 1 Kings 17:18). Jehu refuses to answer the king's question and takes the messenger under his own command.

decisions.choice: turn around behind me: join my troop
decisions.reason: Jehu orders the rider to turn and ride behind him. The messenger goes over to Jehu's side and cannot return with news.

decisions.choice: is it peace?: as in verse 17
decisions.reason: The king's question is passed on in his own words.

decisions.choice: Fall in behind me (Balanced); Turn around and follow me (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the military command (m2).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח רֹכֵ֣ב סוּס֮ שֵׁנִי֒ וַיָּבֹ֣א אֲלֵהֶ֔ם וַיֹּ֛אמֶר כֹּֽה־אָמַ֥ר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ שָׁל֑וֹם וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יֵה֛וּא מַה־לְּךָ֥ וּלְשָׁל֖וֹם סֹ֥ב אֶֽל־אַחֲרָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he sent a rider of a horse, a second, and he came to them and said, Thus says the king, Peace? And said Jehu, What [is it] to you and to peace? Turn to behind me.

en.L: And he sent a second rider on a horse, and he came to them and said, "Thus says the king: 'Is it peace?'" And Jehu said, "What [is it] to you and to peace? Turn around behind me."
en.B: Then Joram sent a second horseman. He came to them and said, "The king says this: 'Is it peace?'" Jehu said, "What business of yours is peace? Fall in behind me."
en.R: Then King Joram sent out a second man on a horse. He came to them and said, "The king asks, 'Do you come in peace?'" Jehu answered, "What does peace matter to you? Turn around and follow me."

decisions.choice: peace?: a question without the question marker
decisions.reason: This time the Hebrew has the word "peace" without the small word that marks a question, but in this setting it is the same question as in verses 17-18; the tone of voice made it a question.

decisions.choice: the same answer: as in verse 18
decisions.reason: Jehu's reply is word for word what he said to the first rider; the repetition shows the second messenger meets the same fate.

decisions.choice: Joram
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the king who sent the second rider.

source.text: וַיַּגֵּ֤ד הַצֹּפֶה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּ֥א עַד־אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וְלֹֽא־שָׁ֑ב וְהַמִּנְהָ֗ג כְּמִנְהַג֙ יֵה֣וּא בֶן־נִמְשִׁ֔י כִּ֥י בְשִׁגָּע֖וֹן יִנְהָֽג׃

records.literal_gloss: And reported the watchman, saying, He came to them and not returned; and the driving [is] like [the] driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for in madness he drives.

en.L: And the watchman reported, saying, "He came to them, but he has not returned. And the driving [is] like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives in madness."
en.B: The watchman reported again, "He reached them, but he is not coming back either. And the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives like a madman."
en.R: The guard reported, "He reached them too, but he is not coming back either. The leader drives his chariot wildly, like a madman. It must be Jehu son of Nimshi!"

decisions.choice: he drives in madness: he drives wildly, recklessly
decisions.reason: The word means madness, wild behavior. Jehu was known for driving his chariot hard and fast, and the watchman knows him by it from far off. The word comes from the same root as "madman" in verse 11: the officers called the prophet mad, and now Jehu is the one driving like a madman.

decisions.choice: Jehu son of Nimshi: named by his grandfather
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, Jehu is called by the name of his better-known grandfather.

decisions.choice: It must be Jehu son of Nimshi!
decisions.reason: Readable puts the watchman's conclusion last, after the wild driving that let him recognize Jehu.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוֹרָם֙ אֱסֹ֔ר וַיֶּאְסֹ֖ר רִכְבּ֑וֹ וַיֵּצֵ֣א יְהוֹרָ֣ם מֶֽלֶךְ־יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל וַאֲחַזְיָ֨הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֜ה אִ֣ישׁ בְּרִכְבּ֗וֹ וַיֵּֽצְאוּ֙ לִקְרַ֣את יֵה֔וּא וַיִּמְצָאֻ֔הוּ בְּחֶלְקַ֖ת נָב֥וֹת הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Joram, Harness! And one harnessed his chariot, and went out Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah, each in his chariot, and they went out to meet Jehu, and they found him in [the] plot of Naboth the Jezreelite.

en.L: And Jehoram said, "Harness [it]!" And his chariot was harnessed, and Jehoram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot. And they went out to meet Jehu, and they found him on the plot of ground of Naboth the Jezreelite.
en.B: Jehoram said, "Hitch up my chariot!" When his chariot was ready, Jehoram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah rode out, each in his own chariot, to meet Jehu, and they met him on the plot of ground that had belonged to Naboth the Jezreelite.
en.R: "Get my chariot ready!" Jehoram ordered. When it was ready, King Jehoram of Israel and King Ahaziah of Judah rode out, each in his own chariot, to meet Jehu. They met him at the field that had once belonged to Naboth, the man from Jezreel.

decisions.choice: harness: get the chariot ready
decisions.reason: The verb means to tie or bind, here to hitch the horses to the chariot (1 Kings 18:44).

decisions.choice: they found him on the plot of ground of Naboth: the place of Ahab's crime
decisions.reason: This is the vineyard Ahab took after Jezebel had Naboth killed (1 Kings 21:1-16). Elijah had said that Yahweh would repay Ahab's house on that very ground (1 Kings 21:19-24); verses 25-26 make the link.

decisions.choice: found him: met him
decisions.reason: The verb means to find or to meet; the kings came upon Jehu there, which the narrator does not present as chance.

decisions.choice: that had belonged to Naboth (Balanced); that had once belonged to Naboth (Readable)
decisions.reason: Naboth was dead and his land had been taken by Ahab (1 Kings 21:16). Balanced and Readable make this plain.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י כִּרְא֤וֹת יְהוֹרָם֙ אֶת־יֵה֔וּא וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הֲשָׁל֣וֹם יֵה֑וּא וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ מָ֣ה הַשָּׁל֔וֹם עַד־זְנוּנֵ֞י אִיזֶ֧בֶל אִמְּךָ֛ וּכְשָׁפֶ֖יהָ הָרַבִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when saw Joram Jehu, and he said, [Is it] peace, Jehu? And he said, What peace, as long as [the] prostitutions of Jezebel your mother and her sorceries [are] many?

en.L: And it happened, when Jehoram saw Jehu, that he said, "Is it peace, Jehu?" And he said, "What peace, as long as the prostitutions of Jezebel your mother and her sorceries [are] many?"
en.B: When Jehoram saw Jehu, he said, "Is it peace, Jehu?" Jehu answered, "How can there be peace, as long as the prostitutions and the many sorceries of your mother Jezebel go on?"
en.R: When Jehoram saw Jehu, he called out, "Do you come in peace, Jehu?" Jehu answered, "How can there be peace while your mother Jezebel leads the people to worship idols and uses so much witchcraft?"

decisions.choice: is it peace?: as in verse 17
decisions.reason: The king himself now asks the question his messengers carried, and Jehu answers it.

decisions.choice: the prostitutions of Jezebel: her unfaithfulness to Yahweh in worshiping other gods
decisions.reason: The prophets call the worship of other gods prostitution, since Israel belonged to Yahweh as a wife to her husband (Exodus 34:15-16; Hosea 1:2; 4:12). Jezebel brought the worship of Baal into Israel (1 Kings 16:31-32; 18:19). The charge is idolatry, not her personal conduct.

decisions.choice: sorceries: magic and occult practice
decisions.reason: The word is used of spells and magic forbidden in Israel (Deuteronomy 18:10; Micah 5:11). It may be meant figuratively for the lure of her religion, or of real magic practiced in the worship she promoted.

decisions.choice: what peace, as long as ...: peace is impossible while this goes on
decisions.reason: Jehu turns the king's question back on him: there can be no peace while the queen mother's idolatry continues.

decisions.choice: leads the people to worship idols; uses so much witchcraft
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain sense of "prostitutions" (m2) and uses a familiar word for sorcery. The word "prostitutions" at Literal and Balanced keeps the prophets' picture of unfaithfulness.

source.text: וַיַּהֲפֹ֧ךְ יְהוֹרָ֛ם יָדָ֖יו וַיָּנֹ֑ס וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֶל־אֲחַזְיָ֖הוּ מִרְמָ֥ה אֲחַזְיָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And turned Joram his hands and fled, and he said to Ahaziah, Treachery, Ahaziah!

en.L: And Jehoram turned his hands and fled, and he said to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"
en.B: Jehoram turned his chariot around and fled, calling out to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"
en.R: Jehoram turned his chariot around and tried to escape. He shouted to Ahaziah, "It is a trap, Ahaziah!"

decisions.choice: turned his hands: turned the chariot around
decisions.reason: The hands hold the reins, so to turn the hands is to wheel the chariot about (1 Kings 22:34).

decisions.choice: treachery: betrayal
decisions.reason: The word means deceit or betrayal. Jehoram sees that his own commander has risen against him.

decisions.choice: turned his chariot around
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom (m1).

decisions.choice: It is a trap
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jehoram meant by "treachery" in plain words.

source.text: וְיֵה֞וּא מִלֵּ֧א יָד֣וֹ בַקֶּ֗שֶׁת וַיַּ֤ךְ אֶת־יְהוֹרָם֙ בֵּ֣ין זְרֹעָ֔יו וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַחֵ֖צִי מִלִּבּ֑וֹ וַיִּכְרַ֖ע בְּרִכְבּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And Jehu filled his hand with the bow and struck Joram between his arms, and came out the arrow from his heart, and he sank down in his chariot.

en.L: And Jehu filled his hand with the bow and struck Jehoram between his arms, and the arrow went out through his heart, and he sank down in his chariot.
en.B: Jehu drew his bow with all his strength and shot Jehoram between the shoulders. The arrow went through his heart, and he slumped down in his chariot.
en.R: Jehu pulled back his bow as far as it would go and shot Jehoram in the back, between the shoulders. The arrow went right through his heart, and he fell down dead in his chariot.

decisions.choice: filled his hand with the bow: drew the bow to its full stretch
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means Jehu bent the bow with full strength (compare Zechariah 9:13). It could also mean that he took the bow in hand.

decisions.choice: between his arms: between the shoulders, in the back
decisions.reason: The word means arms, and the shot struck Jehoram between them from behind as he fled (verse 23).

decisions.choice: he sank down: he collapsed, dead
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow down or sink to the knees; here Jehoram falls dying in his chariot.

decisions.choice: drew his bow with all his strength (Balanced); pulled back his bow as far as it would go (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֶל־בִּדְקַר֙ שָֽׁלִשׁ֔וֹ שָׂ֚א הַשְׁלִכֵ֔הוּ בְּחֶלְקַ֕ת שְׂדֵ֖ה נָב֣וֹת הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֑י כִּֽי־זְכֹ֞ר אֲנִ֣י וָאַ֗תָּה אֵ֣ת רֹכְבִ֤ים צְמָדִים֙ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ אַחְאָ֣ב אָבִ֔יו וַֽיהוָה֙ נָשָׂ֣א עָלָ֔יו אֶת־הַמַּשָּׂ֖א הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to Bidkar his officer, Lift [him] up, throw him in [the] plot of [the] field of Naboth the Jezreelite; for remember, I and you [were] riding pairs behind Ahab his father, and Yahweh lifted up against him this oracle:

en.L: And he said to Bidkar his officer, "Lift [him] up [and] throw him on the plot of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite, for remember how I and you were riding in pairs behind Ahab his father, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lifted up against him this oracle:
en.B: Jehu said to his officer Bidkar, "Pick him up and throw him on the plot of ground that was Naboth the Jezreelite's field. Remember how you and I were riding side by side behind his father Ahab, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke this oracle against him:
en.R: Jehu said to Bidkar, his officer, "Pick up his body and throw it into the field that belonged to Naboth from Jezreel. Do you remember when you and I were riding together behind Joram's father Ahab? That was when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke this message against Ahab:

decisions.choice: his officer: an aide, perhaps the third man in the chariot
decisions.reason: The word is related to the number three. It may name the third man who rode in a war chariot, or more generally a high officer or aide to a king or commander (7:2; 1 Kings 9:22).

decisions.choice: riding in pairs: riding side by side in chariots
decisions.reason: The word means a pair or team; Jehu and Bidkar rode together, perhaps in one chariot or in chariots side by side, in Ahab's escort.

decisions.choice: lifted up this oracle: pronounced this solemn word
decisions.reason: The word for oracle comes from the verb "lift up" and means a pronouncement, a weighty message of judgment (Isaiah 13:1). Jehu remembers Elijah's word against Ahab at Naboth's vineyard (1 Kings 21:17-24).

decisions.choice: behind Ahab his father: Jehu had heard Elijah's word himself
decisions.reason: Jehu says he was in Ahab's company when Elijah met the king (1 Kings 21:17-19). What he does now carries out a word he heard with his own ears.

decisions.choice: Joram's father Ahab
decisions.reason: Readable names Joram, since "his" could be unclear.

source.text: אִם־לֹ֡א אֶת־דְּמֵ֣י נָבוֹת֩ וְאֶת־דְּמֵ֨י בָנָ֜יו רָאִ֤יתִי אֶ֨מֶשׁ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְשִׁלַּמְתִּ֥י לְךָ֛ בַּחֶלְקָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְעַתָּ֗ה שָׂ֧א הַשְׁלִכֵ֛הוּ בַּחֶלְקָ֖ה כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Surely [the] blood of Naboth and [the] blood of his sons I saw yesterday, declares Yahweh, and I will repay you on this plot, declares Yahweh. And now lift [him] up, throw him on the plot according to [the] word of Yahweh.

en.L: 'Surely I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons yesterday, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I will repay you on this plot of ground, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.' So now lift [him] up [and] throw him on the plot of ground, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.B: 'I surely saw the blood of Naboth and of his sons yesterday, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I will repay you on this plot of ground, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.' So now pick him up and throw him on that plot of ground, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said."
en.R: 'Yesterday I saw the blood of Naboth and of his sons, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And I will surely punish you for it on this same piece of land, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.' So pick up Joram's body and throw it onto that land, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said."

decisions.choice: surely: the form of an oath
decisions.reason: The words "if not" begin a solemn oath, meaning "I swear that" (1 Samuel 3:14). Yahweh binds himself to repay.

decisions.choice: the blood of Naboth and of his sons, yesterday: more than 1 Kings 21 tells
decisions.reason: The account in 1 Kings 21:13 tells only of Naboth's death. Jehu's words show that his sons were killed too, so that no heir was left to claim the land. "Yesterday" means the day before Elijah spoke (1 Kings 21:17-18).

decisions.choice: I will repay you on this plot of ground: Elijah's word fulfilled
decisions.reason: Elijah had said that where the dogs licked Naboth's blood they would lick Ahab's (1 Kings 21:19). Because Ahab humbled himself, the disaster was put off to his son's days (1 Kings 21:29). Now Ahab's son lies on Naboth's ground.

decisions.choice: declares the LORD (Literal, Balanced); says the LORD (Readable)
decisions.reason: As settled for Samuel and Kings.

decisions.choice: as the LORD said
decisions.reason: "According to the word of the LORD" is put in plainer words at Balanced and Readable.

source.text: וַאֲחַזְיָ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ רָאָ֔ה וַיָּ֕נָס דֶּ֖רֶךְ בֵּ֣ית הַגָּ֑ן וַיִּרְדֹּ֨ף אַחֲרָ֜יו יֵה֗וּא וַ֠יֹּאמֶר גַּם־אֹת֞וֹ הַכֻּ֣הוּ אֶל־הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֗ה בְּמַֽעֲלֵה־גוּר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֶֽת־יִבְלְעָ֔ם וַיָּ֥נָס מְגִדּ֖וֹ וַיָּ֥מָת שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And Ahaziah king of Judah saw and fled [by the] way of Beth-haggan; and pursued after him Jehu and said, Also him strike him, in the chariot, at [the] ascent of Gur which [is] by Ibleam; and he fled [to] Megiddo and died there.

en.L: And Ahaziah king of Judah saw [it] and fled by the way of Beth-haggan. And Jehu pursued him and said, "Him too, strike him!" [And they struck him] in the chariot at the ascent of Gur, which [is] by Ibleam. And he fled to Megiddo and died there.
en.B: When Ahaziah king of Judah saw this, he fled along the road to Beth-haggan. Jehu chased him and said, "Shoot him too!" They shot him in his chariot on the way up to Gur, near Ibleam, but he escaped to Megiddo and died there.
en.R: When King Ahaziah of Judah saw what happened, he fled toward the town of Beth-haggan. Jehu chased him and shouted, "Shoot him too!" So they shot him in his chariot on the road that goes up to Gur, near the town of Ibleam. Ahaziah got away to Megiddo, but he died there.

decisions.choice: strike him in the chariot: the command and its carrying out
alternatives: Strike him too in the chariot at the ascent of Gur (all part of the command)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives Jehu's command and then the place where Ahaziah was hit, without a verb saying that the men obeyed. It is most likely a short way of telling that they shot him there.

decisions.choice: Beth-haggan, Gur, Ibleam, Megiddo: south and west from Jezreel
decisions.reason: Beth-haggan means "house of the garden". Ahaziah fled south toward Judah, was wounded on the climb near Ibleam, and turned aside to Megiddo, where he died.

decisions.choice: he died there: a different account in Chronicles
decisions.reason: 2 Chronicles 22:9 tells Ahaziah's death in another way, saying he was found hiding in Samaria and brought to Jehu. The two accounts are told from different sources and do not explain each other.

decisions.choice: They shot him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the action the Hebrew leaves implied (m1); Literal puts it in brackets.

source.text: וַיַּרְכִּ֧בוּ אֹת֛וֹ עֲבָדָ֖יו יְרוּשָׁלְָ֑מָה וַיִּקְבְּר֨וּ אֹת֧וֹ בִקְבֻרָת֛וֹ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֖יו בְּעִ֥יר דָּוִֽד׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And carried him his servants in a chariot to Jerusalem and buried him in his grave with his fathers in [the] city of David.

en.L: And his servants carried him in a chariot to Jerusalem and buried him in his grave with his fathers in the City of David.
en.B: His officials took him to Jerusalem in a chariot and buried him with his ancestors in his tomb in the City of David.
en.R: His officials carried his body in a chariot to Jerusalem. They buried him in his tomb with his ancestors in the City of David.

decisions.choice: carried him in a chariot: made him ride
decisions.reason: The verb means "made him ride"; the body was taken home in a chariot.

decisions.choice: buried with his fathers in the City of David: a royal burial
decisions.reason: Unlike Joram and Jezebel, Ahaziah received a king's burial in the family tomb in Jerusalem (8:24).

decisions.choice: servants (Literal); officials (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The king's servants are his court officials, as settled for Samuel and Kings.

source.text: וּבִשְׁנַת֙ אַחַ֣ת עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹרָ֖ם בֶּן־אַחְאָ֑ב מָלַ֥ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֖ה עַל־יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And in year one [and] ten year of Joram son of Ahab had become king Ahaziah over Judah.

en.L: And in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, Ahaziah had become king over Judah.
en.B: Ahaziah had become king over Judah in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab.
en.R: Ahaziah had become king of Judah in the eleventh year that Joram son of Ahab was king of Israel.

decisions.choice: had become king: a note looking back
decisions.reason: The narrator adds a note on when Ahaziah's reign began, closing the account of his life.

decisions.choice: the eleventh year: one year apart from 8:25
decisions.reason: 8:25 dates Ahaziah's accession to Joram's twelfth year. The difference probably comes from two ways of counting a king's years, with or without the part year in which he came to the throne.

decisions.choice: that Joram son of Ahab was king of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says that the years are counted from Joram's reign in Israel.

source.text: וַיָּב֥וֹא יֵה֖וּא יִזְרְעֶ֑אלָה וְאִיזֶ֣בֶל שָׁמְעָ֗ה וַתָּ֨שֶׂם בַּפּ֤וּךְ עֵינֶ֨יהָ֙ וַתֵּ֣יטֶב אֶת־רֹאשָׁ֔הּ וַתַּשְׁקֵ֖ף בְּעַ֥ד הַחַלּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Jehu [to] Jezreel, and Jezebel heard, and she put in eye-paint her eyes and made good her head and looked down through the window.

en.L: And Jehu came to Jezreel, and Jezebel heard [of it], and she put her eyes in paint and adorned her head, and looked down through the window.
en.B: Then Jehu came to Jezreel. When Jezebel heard of it, she painted her eyes, arranged her hair and looked down from the window.
en.R: Then Jehu arrived in Jezreel. When Jezebel heard he was coming, she put on eye makeup and fixed her hair. Then she looked down from an upstairs window.

decisions.choice: she painted her eyes: she put on dark eye paint
decisions.reason: Women outlined their eyes with a dark powder made from minerals (Jeremiah 4:30; Ezekiel 23:40).

decisions.choice: adorned her head and looked down through the window: she met Jehu as a queen
decisions.reason: Jezebel prepared herself with royal dignity, perhaps putting on her headdress, and faced Jehu from the palace window. The text does not say she meant to seduce him; her words in verse 31 are scorn, not welcome. She meets death as a queen.

decisions.choice: looked down: looked out from above
decisions.reason: The verb is used of looking down from a height or a window (Judges 5:28; 2 Samuel 6:16). The window was in an upper room of the palace.

decisions.choice: painted her eyes, arranged her hair (Balanced); put on eye makeup and fixed her hair (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Made good her head" means she did her hair or headdress; Balanced and Readable say it in plain words.

source.text: וְיֵה֖וּא בָּ֣א בַשָּׁ֑עַר וַתֹּ֣אמֶר הֲשָׁל֔וֹם זִמְרִ֖י הֹרֵ֥ג אֲדֹנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And Jehu came in the gate, and she said, [Is it] peace, Zimri, murderer of his master?

en.L: And Jehu came in at the gate, and she said, "Is it peace, Zimri, murderer of his master?"
en.B: As Jehu came in through the gate, she said, "Is it peace, you Zimri, murderer of your master?"
en.R: As Jehu came through the city gate, she called out, "Do you come in peace, you Zimri? You murdered your master!"

decisions.choice: Zimri, murderer of his master: a taunt
decisions.reason: Zimri, a chariot commander, killed his king Elah and took the throne, but he reigned only seven days before Omri, Ahab's father, besieged him and he died in the burning palace (1 Kings 16:9-18). Jezebel calls Jehu "Zimri" to warn him that a traitor's reign does not last.

decisions.choice: is it peace?: mockery
decisions.reason: Jezebel asks the question the messengers and the king had asked (verses 17-22), now with scorn. She knows he has not come in peace.

decisions.choice: murderer of his master: said of Jehu, spoken to him
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "his master", as a title for the man addressed; it means Jehu, who has just killed his master Joram.

decisions.choice: your master
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "your", since Jezebel is speaking to Jehu (m3); Literal keeps "his".

source.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֤א פָנָיו֙ אֶל־הַ֣חַלּ֔וֹן וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מִ֥י אִתִּ֖י מִ֑י וַיַּשְׁקִ֣יפוּ אֵלָ֔יו שְׁנַ֥יִם שְׁלֹשָׁ֖ה סָרִיסִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he lifted his face to the window and said, Who [is] with me? Who? And looked down to him two [or] three eunuchs.

en.L: And he lifted his face to the window and said, "Who [is] with me? Who?" And two [or] three eunuchs looked down at him.
en.B: Jehu looked up at the window. "Who is on my side?" he called. "Who?" Two or three officials looked down at him.
en.R: Jehu looked up toward the window and shouted, "Who is with me? Who?" Two or three palace officials looked down at him.

decisions.choice: eunuchs: palace officials, probably castrated servants
decisions.reason: The word can mean a castrated man or, more generally, a court official. In the women's quarters of a palace the queen's attendants were often eunuchs, and that may be the sense here (compare Esther 2:3; 4:5).

decisions.choice: who is with me? who?: who will take my side?
decisions.reason: Jehu calls for anyone in the palace willing to turn against Jezebel.

decisions.choice: eunuchs (Literal); officials (Balanced); palace officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: As settled for Samuel and Kings; the footnote gives the narrower sense (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר שִׁמְט֖וּהָ וַֽיִּשְׁמְט֑וּהָ וַיִּ֨ז מִדָּמָ֧הּ אֶל־הַקִּ֛יר וְאֶל־הַסּוּסִ֖ים וַֽיִּרְמְסֶֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Let her drop! And they let her drop, and spattered some of her blood on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled her.

en.L: And he said, "Let her drop!" And they let her drop, and some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled her.
en.B: "Throw her down!" he said. They threw her down, and some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and Jehu drove over her.
en.R: "Throw her down!" Jehu ordered. So they threw her down. Some of her blood splashed onto the wall and onto the horses, and Jehu drove his horses over her body.

decisions.choice: let her drop: throw her down
decisions.reason: The verb means to let fall or release; the officials threw her from the window.

decisions.choice: he trampled her: Jehu drove his horses and chariot over her
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he", meaning Jehu, whose horses and chariot went over her body. Some ancient translations read "they trampled her", meaning the horses.

decisions.choice: Jehu drove over her (Balanced); drove his horses over her body (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jehu and say how he trampled her (m2).

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֖א וַיֹּ֣אכַל וַיֵּ֑שְׁתְּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר פִּקְדוּ־נָ֞א אֶת־הָאֲרוּרָ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ וְקִבְר֔וּהָ כִּ֥י בַת־מֶ֖לֶךְ הִֽיא׃

records.literal_gloss: And he went in and ate and drank, and he said, Attend please to the cursed [woman] this, and bury her, for daughter of a king she [is].

en.L: And he went in and ate and drank, and he said, "Please attend to this cursed [woman] and bury her, for she [is] a king's daughter."
en.B: Then Jehu went in and ate and drank. He said, "See to this cursed woman and bury her, for she was a king's daughter."
en.R: Then Jehu went into the palace and had something to eat and drink. Later he said, "Take care of that cursed woman and bury her. After all, she was a king's daughter."

decisions.choice: this cursed woman: under Yahweh's curse
decisions.reason: The word means one on whom a curse rests. Jezebel had fallen under the curse Elijah spoke (1 Kings 21:23).

decisions.choice: a king's daughter: born to royalty
decisions.reason: Jezebel was the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians (1 Kings 16:31). Jehu means to give her the burial due to royal birth, but it is already too late (verses 35-37).

decisions.choice: he went in and ate and drank: Jehu takes possession of the palace
decisions.reason: Jehu enters the royal house and eats there as its new master, while Jezebel's body lies outside.

decisions.choice: into the palace; Later
decisions.reason: Readable says where Jehu went and that the order came after the meal.

source.text: וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ לְקָבְרָ֑הּ וְלֹא־מָ֣צְאוּ בָ֗הּ כִּ֧י אִם־הַגֻּלְגֹּ֛לֶת וְהָרַגְלַ֖יִם וְכַפּ֥וֹת הַיָּדָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they went to bury her, and not they found of her except the skull and the feet and the palms of the hands.

en.L: And they went to bury her, but they did not find [anything] of her except the skull and the feet and the palms of the hands.
en.B: But when they went to bury her, they found nothing of her except her skull, her feet and the palms of her hands.
en.R: But when the men went to bury her, all they found was her skull, her feet and her hands.

decisions.choice: the skull, the feet and the palms of the hands: the dogs had eaten the rest
decisions.reason: Only the parts the scavenging dogs left were found, as verse 36 makes clear. Elijah's word that she would not be buried came true (verse 10).

decisions.choice: her hands
decisions.reason: Readable shortens "the palms of the hands" to "her hands".

en.B: They went back and told Jehu, and he said, "This is the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Elijah the Tishbite: 'The dogs will eat the flesh of Jezebel on the plot of ground at Jezreel,

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh spoken by Elijah: fulfilled
decisions.reason: Elijah had said, "The dogs will eat Jezebel by the rampart of Jezreel" (1 Kings 21:23). Jehu quotes the word in a form close to verse 10, with "plot of ground" and "flesh".

decisions.choice: by the hand of his servant: through his servant
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" means through someone, as the one who carries the message (1 Kings 14:18; 16:7).

decisions.choice: the Tishbite: from Tishbe
decisions.reason: Elijah came from Tishbe in Gilead (1 Kings 17:1).

decisions.choice: slave (Literal); servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

decisions.choice: Dogs will eat Jezebel's body on the land at Jezreel.

records.literal_gloss: and will be [the] corpse of Jezebel like dung on [the] face of the field in [the] plot of Jezreel, so that not they will say, This [is] Jezebel.

en.L: and the corpse of Jezebel will be like dung on the face of the field in the plot of ground of Jezreel, so that they will not say, "This [is] Jezebel."'"
en.B: and the corpse of Jezebel will be like dung on the surface of the field in the plot of ground at Jezreel, so that no one will be able to say, "This is Jezebel."'"
en.R: Her body will be like manure spread on a field at Jezreel, so that no one will be able to say, "This is Jezebel."'"

decisions.choice: like dung on the face of the field: left unburied and despised
decisions.reason: The picture of corpses lying like manure on the ground is used by the prophets for those who die under judgment and are not buried or mourned (Jeremiah 8:2; 9:21; 16:4; Psalm 83:11). Elijah's words in 1 Kings 21:23 are given more fully here.

decisions.choice: so that they will not say, This is Jezebel: no grave or body will remain
decisions.reason: Nothing will be left to mark her, no tomb and no body to name. The proud queen will vanish without a memorial.

decisions.choice: will be: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) have an older spelling of this verb; the form marked to be read aloud (qere) is the usual one. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: manure spread on a field
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain word for dung and says how it lies on a field.
